newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Parent to continue boosting China Travel -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Parent to continue boosting China Travel -- paper.

text.p: China Travel Service (Holdings) Hong Kong Ltd plans to keep injecting assets into China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd (CTII) to boost its market capitalisation, the South China Morning Post said.
China Travel Service aimed to push its listed arm's market capitalisation to HK$100 billion from HK$10 billion, the newspaper reported on Thursday.
"We want the size of CTII to be like other large listed red chips," the daily quoted Zhu Yuening, chairman of China Travel Service and China Travel International, as saying.
It said Zhu did not give a timeframe for the expansion.
Zhu also said China Travel International was planning to spin off its hotel business in the near future, the newspaper said.

The company has three hotels in Hong Kong and the parent company owned another three in Hong Kong, one in Macau and 11 in China. The total asset value of the hotels was about HK$5-6 billion and the group planned to acquire more, the South China Morning Post said.
China Travel International raised about HK$2.5 billion in a share placement earlier this month and the company had more than HK$3 billion cash on hand, Zhu said.
